articles.headline: Manage end‑user OAuth consent for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
articles.dek: Amazon adds a built‑in consent portal to Bedrock AgentCore, letting end users approve third‑party service access before an AI agent runs a tool.

body.text: Key Takeaway

AgentCore now ships a built‑in OAuth consent portal that captures end‑user approval before an AI agent invokes an external tool [FACT:6f2ef1c41f75113b78b80e5f89d745f3][FACT:93b7c54a26b9ee0df641475653cd9ab4]. Admins turn it on in the Bedrock console; no code changes are required [FACT:f4843624256dea1afc55d943729a3c31].
Why This Matters

GitHub‑hosted agents frequently need credentials to call external APIs, so they either embed tokens or fail when access is revoked [FACT:9435e036cbca9aaddf31b969d6b9c7c9]. Delegating consent to the user’s identity provider satisfies compliance rules and removes the need for hard‑coded secrets [FACT:c8f4814bdfc2bb97ce8f8e0cd4438d96][FACT:7e00a2f787e88291ca1a859dfb1afec7].
What Happened

Amazon expanded the AgentCore identity capability with a new consent portal, reachable from the Bedrock console’s “OAuth Consent” tab [FACT:6f2ef1c41f75113b78b80e5f89d745f3]. When a user starts a tool, the portal redirects the browser to the organization’s IdP, binds the session, and returns an OAuth token for the agent to use [FACT:c8f4814bdfc2bb97ce8f8e0cd4438d96][FACT:7e00a2f787e88291ca1a859dfb1afec7]. Admins define which scopes each tool may request, and the console logs every consent event for audit purposes [FACT:f4843624256dea1afc55d943729a3c31][FACT:11f628e57447b148dae09f3941d8ab9e].
Builder View

If you already run Bedrock AgentCore, enable the “OAuth Consent” switch to protect your API keys—existing agents will automatically use the new flow without code changes [FACT:11f628e57447b148dae09f3941d8ab9e][FACT:6f2ef1c41f75113b78b80e5f89d745f3]. Agents that use the Model Context Protocol receive the token in the request context, matching the protocol’s design for tool calls [FACT:cecb5a629f313d3ebcfa793abed89845].
Ardur Take

Two independent AWS communications confirm the feature, its console UI, and the preview rollout; confidence in the implementation is high [FACT:6f2ef1c41f75113b78b80e5f89d745f3][FACT:f4843624256dea1afc55d943729a3c31].

keyPoints: AgentCore identity now includes an OAuth consent portal [FACT:6f2ef1c41f75113b78b80e5f89d745f3].
End users grant consent via their organization’s IdP before an agent calls an external service [FACT:c8f4814bdfc2bb97ce8f8e0cd4438d96][FACT:93b7c54a26b9ee0df641475653cd9ab4].
Admins configure scopes and review consent logs directly in the Bedrock Management Console [FACT:f4843624256dea1afc55d943729a3c31].
articles.whyItMatters: Secure token handling and auditability are mandatory for production AI agents that call external APIs; the new consent portal satisfies both requirements out of the box [FACT:9435e036cbca9aaddf31b969d6b9c7c9][FACT:11f628e57447b148dae09f3941d8ab9e].
articles.readerAction: Open the Bedrock console, go to the ‘OAuth Consent’ section under AgentCore, and follow the wizard to define scopes and test a user flow [FACT:f4843624256dea1afc55d943729a3c31].
